terms.grammar: uxor, uxōris f., with poscō, poscere, poposcī; the woman in the accusative, the man in the dative
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 219: fīliam tuam mī uxōrem poscō
Plaut. Trin. 499: sine dōte poscō tuam sorōrem fīliō
terms.comment: Lewis & Short, s.v. poscō: “to demand one’s hand, ask in marriage”. The request went to the woman’s father, who promised her (dēspondēre).

evidence: Plaut. Aul. 237: tū condiciōnem hanc accipe
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a marriage, match … (freq. and class.)”; in full, condiciō uxōria (Cic. Lael. 34).

terms.gloss: promise in marriage (of the father); accept a proposal
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 238: atque eam dēspondē mī

phrases.latin: quae rēs rēctē vortat mihique tibique tuaeque fīliae, fīliam tuam mī uxōrem poscō. prōmitte hoc fore.
phrases.english: And may it turn out well for me and for you and for your daughter: I am asking for your daughter’s hand. Promise me it will be so.

phrases.latin: tū condiciōnem hanc accipe, auscultā mihi, atque eam dēspondē mī.
phrases.english: Accept this proposal, listen to me, and promise her to me.

sources: Lewis & Short: posco · Lewis & Short: condicio · Lewis & Short: despondeo
Plaut. Aul. 218–219 and 237–238, Trin. 499–501 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
